misconceptions.description: Believing that using advanced technology is itself an exercise of teacher agency, even when the teacher follows the tool's defaults unchanged
misconceptions.trigger: learner equates running a platform as configured with exercising professional agency
misconceptions.feedback: Agency lives in the deviations you make and can justify, not in operating the tool. Identify where you override or adapt the default for your students.

misconceptions.description: Treating a district mandate as eliminating all professional agency, leaving only full compliance or covert refusal
misconceptions.trigger: learner sees only obey-exactly or quietly-quit when a tool is mandated
misconceptions.feedback: Agency within a mandate means documenting harm, adapting where judgment requires, and feeding evidence back to revise the policy. It is not binary.

misconceptions.description: Delivering AI-generated lesson material as written, ceding authorship and the accountability that comes with it
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats an AI-generated unit as finished rather than a draft to interrogate and revise
misconceptions.feedback: Stay the author of record. Interrogate the draft against your students and curriculum, and keep a record of what you changed and why.

misconceptions.description: Reducing teacher agency to the binary power to turn a tool on or off rather than the capacity to shape how it operates
misconceptions.trigger: learner claims full agency solely because the tool can be disabled
misconceptions.feedback: Go beyond the on/off switch. Real agency is shaping the tool's content, pacing, and limits for specific students, exercised continuously.
